text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Publisher Reed Elsevier buys U.S. firm MDL Information Systems for $320 million, twice its recent market value. (p1)
- KLM Royal Dutch Airlines averted pilot strike last week after postponing decision to use British pilots. (p1)
- Packaging concern Van Leer has doubts about achieving its own target of 15 pct return on capital. (p1)
- Unlisted saving bank SNS completes takeover of Banque de Suez Nederland. (p3)
- Window coverings maker Hunter Douglas takes over Belgian firm Helioscreen. (p3)
- Bathroom equipment producer Sphinx Gustavsberg takes 66 pct stake in Poland's ZWS Wroclaw. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Authorities plan to prosecute soccer hooligans involved in fatal battle on Sunday under law prohibiting membership of a criminal organisation. (p1)
- Record haul of bootleg compact discs at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport. (p2)
- Royal Dutch/Shell again involved in political conflict in Nigeria. (p2)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT makes book profit of 180 million guilders on sale of plastic packaging division to Tenneco. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch central bank warns private investors against the high risks of pyramid investment schemes. (p3)
- Many Dutch people have a phobia for machines and appliances, research shows. (p3)
- Dutch business confidence remains at a high level. (p23)
- Brokerage firm AOT is studying possiblity of developing activities on foreign stock exchanges. (p23)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- KLM targets accelerated growth in the Far East. (p14)
